AI-Driven Sleep Monitoring and Personalized Intervention System for Ovarian Cancer Patients in RGV
CONGRANT.ABSTRACT: Ovarian cancer (OC) often presents with complex sleep disorders during treatments driven by a combination of individual factors (age, socioeconomic status, anxiety), treatment-related factors (pain, cancer stage), and social environmental factors (social support, bedroom environment). Such sleep disorders can adversely affect physical and mental health, hinder treatment outcomes, and eventually reduce patients’ quality of life and survival rates. The se highly individualized and real-time challenges demand precise, adaptable, and continuous monitoring to address them effectively. However, current wearable devices fail to capture real-time measurements with the required qualities. Moreover, integrating wearable device data and patient data is essential for predicting sleep disorders and customizing interventions. We propose an AI-Driven Sleep Monitoring and Personalized Intervention System tailored for OC Patients to address these gaps. This innovative system leverages advanced wearable technology for real-time, continuous monitoring and seamlessly integrates multidimensional data to uncover predictive patterns and deliver tailored, patient-centered interventions. Our research will take place in the resource-limited Rio Grande Valley (RGV) region, where access to healthcare is often constrained. By combining predictive analytics with patient-centered care, this project has the potential to transform sleep quality and significantly improve treatment outcomes for over 200,000 OC patients in the U.S. Moreover, the insights gained from this initiative will offer valuable solutions for similar challenges faced in global low-resource settings.

Acquisition of a GPU-Enhanced Advanced Computing and Simulation Instrumentation for Interdisciplinary AI Research and Education at the University of Texas Rio Grande Valley
CONGRANT.ABSTRACT:
(The proposal was a preproposal submitted to UTRGV for an internal competition.)
As UTRGV researchers address critical problems across divers fields that demand the analysis and management of complex, data-intensive problems, the university faces an increasing demand for high-performance computing (HPC) resources to effectively train modern AI models and conduct large-scale simulations. While some HPC resources are available both on and campus, limitations such as long job queues, insufficient graphics processing unit (GPU) memory, and slow interconnects often delay study results by days or force researchers to transfer sensitive data to remote supercomputer facilities. Moreover, while modern large language models (LLMs) are in high demand at UTRGV for a range of applications, existing cloud solutions are costly and pose privacy concerns. To address this gap, the proposal seeks funding to acquire a GPU-Enhanced Advanced Computing and Simulation Instrumentation (GACSI) equipped with the latest NVIDIA B200 GPUs. The B200 GPUs will enable UTRGV to deploy, fine-tune, evaluate, and operate LLMs entirely on campus, significantly reducing waiting times, eliminating cloud-based usage fees, and ensuring the privacy and security of sensitive data. Hosting these models locally will support the development of new hands-on course modules, allowing both undergraduate and graduate students to engage directly with state-of-the-art generative AI.

INTELLCONT.TITLE: Intelligent Battery Performance Prediction based on Deep Learning Algorithm
A Multi‐Disease Detection Method for Paddy Rice Based on Enhancing Detection Transformer With ConvNeXt‐DAM‐FFNet Refinement
INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT: ABSTRACTGlobal food security is seriously threatened by paddy rice diseases, which reduce annual yields in important growing regions. Real‐world field circumstances with complex background interference provide significant obstacles for automated detection systems. Based on the Detection with Transformer methodology, this study offers a unique framework for the identification of plant diseases. Utilising the strong ConvNeXt architecture improves feature extraction, a suggested feature fusion network optimises cross‐level contextual integration, and a deformable attention mechanism permits adaptive spatial localization. The Transformer architecture's structural changes improve the precision of detection. To improve generality, a new optimizer is used to update the model parameters. The Hard‐Swish activation function is also included to improve the model's overall performance by fortifying its capacity to handle nonlinear features. Under varying illumination and occlusion conditions, the experimental evaluation shows superior detection performance with 80.0% precision, 83.2% recall and 81.6% F1‐score with 61.5% mAP on a real field‐collected dataset with 1200 images of four critical paddy rice diseases (bacterial panicle blight, blast, dead heart and hispa). Compared to the baseline model, it shows improvements of 9.3%, 11.9%, 10.6% and 5.5%, respectively. With potential uses in automating agricultural inspection procedures, this study provides a practical and efficient approach for identifying a variety of plant diseases in outdoor settings.

Mid-Infrared Spectrum Sensing Algorithm Applying Micro-Resonator Arrays
Design of mid-infrared cascade micro-ring sensing devices using a machine learning algorithm
INTELLCONT.PUBLISHER: Journal of the Optical Society of America B
INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT: <jats:p>An intelligent mid-infrared (mid-IR) integrated photonic device was demonstrated applying a machine learning (ML) algorithm. The design model and the estimation model of mid-IR micro-rings were trained by the artificial neural network (ANN) to create the performance-structure relationships. The sensing devices were then designed to align the micro-ring resonance with the characteristic mid-IR absorption wavelengths according to the gases of interest. Further applying the cascade micro-ring structures enables the device to monitor several gas analytes simultaneously. The ML-based mid-IR device provides a miniaturized sensing platform for remote and precise environmental monitoring.</jats:p>

INTELLCONT.TITLE: In-Situ Gases Monitoring Using Mid-infrared Gradient Bragg Grating Cavities
INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT: In-Situ gas analysis were illustrated by using mid-Infrared (mid-IR) gradient Bragg grating cavities. Gas mixtures were noninvasively monitored by tracing the characteristic gas absorption bands with algorithmic analysis.

INTELLCONT.TITLE: Real-time isotopic methane detection using mid-infrared spectroscopy
INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT: A real-time, nondestructive mid-infrared (mid-IR) platform was proposed for isotopic methane detection. The measurement system consisted of a tunable mid-IR laser, a miniaturized gas chamber, and a mid-IR signal receiver. The isotope ratio of the 12 C H 4 / 13 C H 4 was identified by measuring the mid-IR spectrum at λ = 3 . 2 − 3 . 5 µ m . In-situ 12 C H 4 / 13 C H 4 monitoring was then achieved by tracing the characteristic mid-IR absorption peaks assigned to the 12 C H 4 at λ = 3.328 µ m and 13 C H 4 at λ = 3.340 µ m . The real-time methane isotope analysis can be applied to environmental monitoring and petroleum industries.
